issues.explanation: down() re-adds unique(queue_id, code) and will fail as soon as a letter has restarted on another day (normal data for this feature), blocking a real rollback; the docblock acknowledges the manual cleanup, but the rollback is not actually runnable on production data.

issue_date is derived from issued_at only in definition(), so a caller-supplied issue_date state can diverge from issued_at, contrary to the requirement that issue_date stays aligned with issued_at for factory-created rows.

The UpdateQueue tests exercise set/keep/invalid/clear but never assert that an unauthorized caller is denied or that priority_prefix_map is rejected by mass assignment, leaving the new write path's security invariants unverified.

No test covers the nullable -> DATE(issued_at) backfill -> NOT NULL -> unique-index swap, so the riskiest part of requirement 3 (and its down()) is untested; the daily-restart test only proves the new index permits the same code on different days.

nextCode mixes three responsibilities (resolving an int prefix by reloading the queue, parsing the day, scanning codes); the factory already has the queue and could pass the resolved letter, avoiding the hidden extra query and the overloaded string|int parameter.

The sequence query plucks every code issued that day for the queue and filters in PHP; filtering by the known letter in SQL (e.g. code LIKE '<prefix>%') would keep busy queues from loading the whole day's codes.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived, per-day ticket codes with a validated per-queue prefix map, the issue_date add/backfill/unique-index migration, factory and issuance updates, tests, and the requested docs; the core logic and edge cases read correctly. I would approve it with nits: the migration's down() cannot roll back once codes repeat across days, an explicit factory issue_date can drift from issued_at, and tests are missing for the migration, mass-assignment, and an unauthorized UpdateQueue call.
